blocks.instruction: Leia o texto e escolha a alternativa correta. Algumas perguntas pedem inferência — a resposta não está escrita com todas as letras.
blocks.passage:
DEI stands for diversity, equity and inclusion — three connected ideas that are often confused. Diversity is the mix of people in the team. Equity is about fair access and opportunities, correcting situations where some groups have been disadvantaged. Inclusion is the daily experience — whether everyone feels they belong and can contribute.

A company can be diverse on paper but not inclusive in practice. You can hire people from many backgrounds and still have meetings where only a few voices are really heard. That is why serious DEI work goes beyond the recruitment step.

Good DEI is not a separate programme run by HR. It is a daily practice — in the way we design meetings, promote people, give feedback and use language. It belongs to every manager, not just to the diversity team.

items.q: According to the text, what is inclusion mainly about?
options: The number of people HR recruits
Whether everyone feels they belong and can contribute
The mix of people in the team
items.why: "Inclusion is the daily experience — whether everyone feels they belong and can contribute."

items.q: How does the text define equity?
options: Correcting situations where some groups have been disadvantaged
Treating every person in exactly the same way
items.why: "Equity is about fair access and opportunities, correcting situations where some groups have been disadvantaged."

items.q: The phrase "diverse on paper but not inclusive in practice" suggests that…
options: recruitment is the only step that matters
HR should own the whole DEI agenda
diversity should not be measured at all
hiring a varied team does not guarantee that everyone is really heard
items.why: Inferência: contratar pessoas variadas não basta se, nas reuniões, só algumas vozes são ouvidas.

items.q: Which statement would the author most likely DISAGREE with?
options: DEI is best handled as a separate programme owned only by HR.
Inclusion is shaped by everyday habits, not only by policies.
A diverse team can still fail to be inclusive.
DEI is the responsibility of every manager.
items.why: Inferência: o texto diz o contrário — "Good DEI is not a separate programme run by HR… It belongs to every manager."

items.q: Why does the author say serious DEI work "goes beyond the recruitment step"?
options: Because who gets hired matters less than the budget
Because recruitment is illegal in some countries
Because HR should never be involved in hiring
Because a diverse hire can still be excluded once inside the company
items.why: Inferência: contratar é só o começo; a experiência diária é que determina se a pessoa é incluída.

blocks.instruction: Ouça Sophie apresentando o relatório anual de DEI ao conselho. Responda sem ler a transcrição — ela só aparece depois de corrigir.

audio.text:
Thank you all for making time. This is the annual DEI report, and I want to be honest about what worked and what didn't.

Let me start with the good news. Our two new affinity groups now have over three hundred members between them, and the feedback has been genuinely warm. People tell us these spaces are the first place they have felt safe to speak openly at work. That is exactly the psychological safety we were aiming for.

Now, what didn't work. We ran unconscious bias training for every manager, but the numbers barely moved in the promotion round that followed. Training alone changes what people say, not always what they do. So next year we are redesigning the promotion process itself — structured criteria, a diverse panel, and clear notes on every decision.

One more thing, and I'll be direct. Being an ally is not a badge you wear; it is something you do every week. I need each of you, at your level, to amplify the voices that don't usually get heard in the room. If the board doesn't model that, no policy of mine will fix it. Questions are welcome.
audio.label: Ouça quantas vezes precisar. A transcrição aparece depois de corrigir.

items.q: What good result does Sophie report first?
options: Every manager was promoted this year
The affinity groups grew and members feel safe to speak openly
The company hired three hundred new staff
The bias training changed all promotion numbers
items.why: "Our two new affinity groups now have over three hundred members… the first place they have felt safe to speak openly."

items.q: What does Sophie say about the unconscious bias training?
options: It changed the promotion numbers a lot
Only a few managers attended it
The numbers barely moved in the promotion round that followed
items.why: "we ran unconscious bias training… but the numbers barely moved in the promotion round that followed."

items.q: What is Sophie's plan for next year?
options: Redesign the promotion process with structured criteria and a diverse panel
Repeat the same training for everyone
items.why: "next year we are redesigning the promotion process itself — structured criteria, a diverse panel, and clear notes."

items.q: When Sophie says "Training alone changes what people say, not always what they do," she implies that…
options: awareness does not automatically change real decisions
training is a waste of money and should stop
items.why: Inferência: a consciência (o que se diz) não muda sozinha o comportamento (o que se faz) — por isso ela vai mudar o processo.

items.q: What is Sophie asking the board members to do?
options: Personally amplify the voices that don't usually get heard
Write the new promotion policy themselves
items.why: Inferência: ela diz que aliança é ação — "amplify the voices that don't usually get heard… If the board doesn't model that, no policy will fix it."

blocks.instruction: O vocabulário da lição aparece aqui em frases novas. Escolha o sentido ou a palavra que cabe no contexto.

items.q: "We rely on structured interviews to reduce unconscious bias." Unconscious bias is…
options: a formal complaint about a manager
an automatic judgement we make without realising it
items.why: Unconscious bias = viés inconsciente: julgamentos automáticos que fazemos sem perceber.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "People do their best work when they feel they truly ___ to the team."
items.why: To belong = pertencer, sentir-se parte — o coração da inclusão.

items.q: Choose the correct term: "An ___ is someone who uses their position to support colleagues from other groups."
items.why: Ally = aliado(a): quem usa sua posição para apoiar colegas de outros grupos.

items.q: "Without psychological safety, people stay silent in meetings." This means the sense that…
options: you can speak up or admit a mistake without being punished
items.why: Psychological safety = segurança psicológica: poder falar ou admitir erros sem medo de punição.

items.q: "The mentoring scheme targets people from an underrepresented group." That is a group that…
options: makes up most of the workforce
works only in the HR department
is present in smaller numbers than its share of the wider population
items.why: Underrepresented group = grupo sub-representado: presente em número menor do que sua proporção na população.

blocks.instruction: Expressões que aparecem em reuniões sobre DEI. Escolha o sentido no contexto.

items.q: "The board still has to sign off on the new inclusion policy." To sign off on means to…
items.why: Sign off on = aprovar formalmente, dar o aval final.

items.q: "We plan to roll out the mentoring scheme across all regions." To roll out means to…
items.why: Roll out = implementar de forma progressiva, região por região.

items.q: "Several managers pushed back on the new quotas." They…
items.why: Push back on = resistir, discordar — sem necessariamente rejeitar de vez.

items.q: "We must follow through on the promises made in last year's report." This means to…
items.why: Follow through = levar até o fim o que foi combinado.

items.q: "A one-off workshop won't move the needle on inclusion." This means it will…
items.why: Move the needle = mexer o ponteiro, fazer diferença perceptível.
